newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh launches crackdown on share manipulators.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh launches crackdown on share manipulators.

text.p: A Bangladeshi court has ordered the arrest of 36 brokers and company owners, including the chairman of the stock exchange, on charges of manipulating share prices, police said on Thursday.

The arrest warrants, including those for exchange chairman Imtiyaz Husain and renowned industrialist Salman Rahman, were issued by the chief metropolitan magistrate on Wednesday night, but police said they had not yet detained any of the suspects.
"We launched an immediate search last night but no one was found at their homes," one police officer said.

Police said the arrest orders were issued after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the watchdog of the country's capital market, filed cases against the suspects for alleged "fraudulent activities" in the capital market.
The cases were filed at the court of the chief metropolitan magistrate on the basis of the report of a four-member inquiry committee headed by Professor Aminul Islam Chowdhury.
The committee was formed on December 26 after stock prices started falling sharply in the wake of a four-month rally, triggering turmoil in the capital market.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) benchmark index was at 1,225.49 on Wednesday, compared with 3,600 in the first week of October.
The stock market started its steep climb soon after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina took power following an election in June 1996.
The DSE index was below 1,000 at the time of the election but rallied afterwards as thousands of people, encouraged by the prospect of political stability, began trading in an unofficial kerb market.
In November, the SEC imposed circuit breakers on price movements to stabilise the market and warned against trading in 24 companies with poor financial track records.
Attorney General K.S. Nabi said the government move was a testimony of its determination to pursue those responsible for the share market scandal.
"The government is giving highest priority to this matter considering the enormous public interest," The Financial Express newspaper quoted Nabi as saying.
SEC chairman Haroonur Rashid told the paper that the SEC would seek the maximum punishment for those responsible for the price manipulation.
"People should feel that discipline is necessary...the general investors should feel confident about the market after the SEC action," Rashid said.
Under SEC rules offenders can be imprisoned for up to five years or fined 500,000 taka ($11,548).
Finance Minister A.S.M.S. Kibria said the country's law would deal with the share market scam and the government's action would have a positive impact on the market.
"I am not moved by any fear or favour in initiating the action," Kibria told The Independent newspaper.

Brokers said on Thursday that the government crackdown could intitially shake investor confidence given the number of major market players on the arrest list. But they said the move would have a positive impact in the longer term and help restore investor confidence.
